title: Fix rubric, note and source-credit layout in exports
body:
Bilingual rubrics could overrun or interrupt reading order, adjacent apparatus marks could overlap, and standalone actor cues could be stranded at the foot of a page before the prayer they introduce. Long source identifiers and URLs could also force horizontal scrolling in mobile electronic books.

Keep standalone cue lines with the following passage, retain spacing decisions when parallel rendering copies notes, and separate whole-note language blocks while preserving foreign words inside running instructions. Group adjacent apparatus marks at their shared anchor without combining their note entries. Set conditional separator rules on their own measured lines so they cannot overhang adjoining rubrics. Remove extra spacing from empty verse markers and optional-clause closers; keep verse numbers tight to attached quotation prefixes. Keep notes targeting explicit body anchors at their anchor instead of hoisting them to a containing division heading; this preserves printed note order. Allow source-credit identifiers and URLs to wrap inside the electronic colophon without changing their link destinations.

Validation:472 XSLT/typography tests and 179 subtests pass, plus the 60-position page-edge geometry sweep with an unprotected control, and a separator test that explicitly rejects overfull hboxes in both single and parallel layouts. Actual documentary and expanded maḥzor extracts verify the cue placement and bilingual rubrics; the expanded extract is byte-identical after narrowing the documentary rule. Independent Claude Opus 5.5 closure review approves the fixes and export QA with no blocking findings. Source evidence records all finite resolutions and exact artifact hashes.

Mobile validation: 130 HTML tests and 176 subtests pass. Three complete electronic books at 390px and 1280px have no horizontal overflow, duplicate IDs, broken internal links or JavaScript errors.

Discovered during #214; kept separate from digitization #296 and opensiddur/opensiddur-projects#102. The maḥzor previews additionally use #312 and #313; #311 is merged.

Final note-order regression: 371 XSLT tests and 152 subtests pass, including a heading/body-anchor case. The full Hebrew preview now keeps all 95 note marks in consecutive order. The targeted independent code review approves the fix.
